first_impression.reaction: Our daughter sent this because she wants my opinion on the walk down the aisle. It's a lovely, calm read, no silly slang, and I know most of these pieces, so I didn't feel old-fashioned for a moment. Short sections, easy on the iPad. It's mostly a song list, so there isn't much here about money, but the destination section near the end asks the right practical questions, including a step-free route for older guests. A few entries just stop mid-sentence, which looks careless.

journey.quote: The walk down the aisle is the shortest part of the ceremony and the one everyone remembers.
journey.reaction: True. I still remember my own. A nice, sensible start.

journey.quote: Recorded music gives you the exact version you love, and needs a reliable sound system, someone to press play and a back-up copy.
journey.reaction: A back-up copy. That's the sort of practical thinking I like. Someone has to be responsible for pressing play.

journey.section: Which classical pieces suit a wedding processional?
journey.quote: The opening movement is bright and sunny,
journey.reaction: The sentence just stops with a comma. If they can't finish a sentence, will they finish the paperwork?

journey.section: What can you walk down the aisle to in a church?
journey.quote: Whether a particular piece, or any secular song, can be used in your church is the church's decision, so ask your officiant or music director early.
journey.reaction: Good, it doesn't pretend. Our parish priest would have views on Ed Sheeran.

journey.section: Which instrumental songs work for the processional?
journey.quote: Its simple, repeating melody is easy to time
journey.reaction: Another one left hanging, no full stop. And 'Married Life' has the same problem. Sloppy for a premium company.

journey.section: What are some modern wedding processional songs?
journey.quote: Rascal Flatts' song spent five weeks at No. 1 on Billboard's Hot Country Songs chart.
journey.reaction: I don't know who these people are. That's the young ones' department. I skimmed the country songs.

journey.section: How does a destination ceremony change your processional music?
journey.quote: How long is the walk on a beach, lawn or clifftop path, and is there a step-free route for older guests?
journey.reaction: Finally, someone thinking of Mum and her walking frame. This is the line I'll show my daughter.

journey.section: How does a destination ceremony change your processional music?
journey.quote: Not published: most venues do not list their sound limits, power at the ceremony site or music permissions online. Your Wedded Advisor confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: In writing, before we commit. That's what I want. But if the musicians don't turn up, whose money is it and who do I ring?

journey.section: Plan the rest of the day's music
journey.quote: When you are ready, tell us your date, your guest list and the feeling you want, and a Wedded Advisor will plan it with you as your single point of contact through Wedded Concierge.
journey.reaction: One person is good. I'd still want a name and a phone call before anything is paid.

unanswered_questions: Who books and pays the musicians overseas, and is that deposit protected if they cancel? (deferred business detail)
Are musicians' fees quoted in AUD and agreed in writing? (deferred business detail)
Who do we ring on the day if the music or sound system fails, and is anyone from Wedded Wonderland there? (deferred business detail)
Is the first conversation a phone call with a real person, and can I join as a parent paying part?
Roughly what does a string quartet or pianist cost for a destination ceremony, From AUD?

turn_offs_found.quote: The opening movement is bright and sunny,
turn_offs_found.why: Unfinished sentences (also 'Its simple, repeating melody is easy to time' and 'It has a light waltz feel and a gentle wit') look careless. If the page is sloppy, I worry the planning will be too.

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
turn_offs_found.why: Good as far as it goes, but nothing says who is responsible for deposits paid to musicians or the venue. My card's turn-off is no mention of deposits or who is accountable.

would_share_with: My daughter, the destination questions list, especially the step-free route line
My husband, the 'in writing before you commit' line, with my question about deposits
My sister, the church section, since she's the one who'll talk to the priest

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, tell us your date, your guest list and the feeling you want, and a Wedded Advisor will plan it with you as your single point of contact through Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: It's warm and not pushy, and one point of contact suits me. But this is a song page; I'd only enquire once my daughter is serious, and I'd want a phone call about deposits, AUD quotes and who we ring on the day.

top_3_changes: Finish the truncated sentences in entries 7, 21 and 28 (Spring, River Flows in You, Married Life); they make the page look unedited.
Next to the destination questions, say in one line who books and pays musicians and how that deposit is handled, only if the business confirms it; otherwise flag.
Add a line in the destination section on who is responsible for the music on the day (who presses play, who to call), sourced from the business or flagged.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent): read top to bottom on iPad, focused on accountability, deposits, older guests and a phone call
No invented brand facts; deposits, AUD fees, on-the-day contact and pricing placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Three entries end mid-sentence (Spring, River Flows in You, Married Life). Can the editor fix these? Also, can the business confirm how musicians' deposits and on-the-day contact are handled for destination ceremonies? If not, flag rather than fill.

assumptions: Margaret arrived via a link from her daughter, reading on an iPad, as a parent contributing about half.
Relevance and enquiry are low because a song list is the couple's decision, not hers; the destination section lifts trust.
Fast mode: full article read top to bottom, modern country entries skimmed as she would.
